quests.sentence: A careful reading of the text revealed what the author had originally intended to convey.
quests.hint: 'Revealed' is past - the reading and its insight are completed events.
quests.explanation: 'Revealed' is the simple past. 'Had intended' is the past perfect. Both are completed past events.

quests.sentence: A careful reading of the text reveals the author's layered and often contradictory true intentions.
quests.hint: 'Reveals' is present - a careful reading currently yields this meaning.
quests.explanation: 'Reveals' is the present simple, describing what a careful current reading of the text yields.

quests.sentence: A careful reading will reveal what the author intended by the deliberately ambiguous final chapter.
quests.hint: 'Will reveal' is the future - the full meaning is still to be uncovered.
quests.explanation: 'Will reveal' is the future simple. The sentence predicts what a future careful reading will yield.

quests.sentence: It was essential that all contracting parties had agreed to every term before the document was signed.
quests.hint: 'Was essential' and 'had agreed' are past - the signing is complete.
quests.explanation: 'Was essential' is the simple past. 'Had agreed' is the past perfect. Both are completed past events.

quests.sentence: It is absolutely essential that all parties fully understand the terms before proceeding to signature.
quests.hint: 'Is essential' and 'understand' are present - this is a current formal requirement.
quests.explanation: 'Is essential' is the present simple. 'Understand' is the present subjunctive base form.

quests.sentence: It will be essential that all parties have reached firm agreement before the contract is finally signed.
quests.hint: 'Will be essential' is the future - the requirement applies to a future signing.
quests.explanation: 'Will be essential' is the future simple. The condition applies to a future event.

quests.sentence: The evidence failed entirely to support the hypothesis that had been so confidently proposed.
quests.hint: 'Failed' is past - the evidence has been assessed and found insufficient.
quests.explanation: 'Failed' is the simple past. 'Had been proposed' is the past perfect. Both are completed past events.

quests.sentence: The evidence does not fully support any of the competing theoretical frameworks currently under consideration.
quests.hint: 'Does not support' is present - this is the current state of the evidence.
quests.explanation: 'Does not support' is the present simple negative. The sentence describes the current state of the evidence.

quests.sentence: The evidence will not be sufficient to draw firm conclusions until the entire study has been completed.
quests.hint: 'Will not be sufficient' is future - the study is not yet complete.
quests.explanation: 'Will not be sufficient' is the future simple. 'Until the study is completed' is a future condition.

quests.sentence: The report that the oversight commission had commissioned directly challenged several long-standing assumptions.
quests.hint: 'Had commissioned' and 'challenged' are past - the report and its findings are completed events.
quests.explanation: 'Had commissioned' is the past perfect. 'Challenged' is the simple past. Both are past events.

quests.sentence: The report that the commission commissions and publishes annually provides essential benchmarking data.
quests.hint: 'Commissions' and 'provides' are present - this is an ongoing annual process.
quests.explanation: 'Commissions' and 'provides' are present simple forms describing a current ongoing process.

quests.sentence: The report that the commission will commission next year is expected to reshape the entire policy landscape.
quests.hint: 'Will commission next year' is future - the report hasn't been commissioned yet.
quests.explanation: 'Will commission' is the future simple. 'Next year' is a clear future time marker.

quests.sentence: What we witnessed together that extraordinary evening was a genuinely and profoundly historic moment.
quests.hint: 'Witnessed' is past - the evening and its events are complete.
quests.explanation: 'Witnessed' is the simple past. 'Was' is also the simple past. The sentence describes a completed past occasion.

quests.sentence: What we witness in our communities every day is the quiet but remarkable strength of human resilience.
quests.hint: 'Witness' and 'is' are present - this is an ongoing observable truth.
quests.explanation: 'Witness' and 'is' are present simple forms. 'Every day' confirms a current ongoing observation.

quests.sentence: What we will achieve together, if we remain committed, is nothing short of truly remarkable.
quests.hint: 'Will achieve' is the future - the achievement is ahead.
quests.explanation: 'Will achieve' is the future simple. The sentence makes a confident prediction about a future collective achievement.

quests.sentence: Her writing demonstrated a rare depth of understanding of human complexity that few contemporaries could match.
quests.hint: 'Demonstrated' and 'could match' are past - this is an assessment of past work.
quests.explanation: 'Demonstrated' is the simple past. 'Could match' is the past modal. Both describe completed past qualities.

quests.sentence: Her writing continues to demonstrate a profound understanding of human nature that resonates with readers worldwide.
quests.hint: 'Continues to demonstrate' is present - her writing has an ongoing current impact.
quests.explanation: 'Continues' is the present simple. The sentence describes the current, ongoing quality and impact of her writing.

quests.sentence: Her writing will reveal to future readers a vivid portrait of the society in which we live today.
quests.hint: 'Will reveal' is the future - the impact on future readers is still to come.
quests.explanation: 'Will reveal' is the future simple. The sentence predicts the future impact of her current writing on future readers.

quests.sentence: The river had been rising steadily for three days before the flood barrier finally gave way.
quests.hint: 'Had been rising' was ongoing before the barrier failing - both are past.
quests.explanation: 'Had been rising' is the past perfect continuous. 'Gave way' is the simple past. Both are past events.

quests.sentence: The river has been rising steadily since Monday and engineers are monitoring it closely around the clock.
quests.hint: 'Has been rising since Monday' spans from the past to the present.
quests.explanation: 'Has been rising' is the present perfect continuous with 'since', showing duration from past to present.

quests.sentence: The river will have been rising for a full week before it finally reaches its predicted dangerous peak.
quests.hint: 'Will have been rising' is the future perfect continuous - duration up to a future point.
quests.explanation: 'Will have been rising' is the future perfect continuous. 'Before it reaches its peak' is a future event.

quests.sentence: What had once seemed utterly impossible had, by the turn of the century, become an entirely routine procedure.
quests.hint: 'Had seemed' and 'had become' are past perfect - both describe a past transformation.
quests.explanation: 'Had seemed' and 'had become' are past perfect forms. The sentence describes a completed past transformation.

quests.sentence: What seems impossible to most people today already exists in prototype form in leading research laboratories.
quests.hint: 'Seems' and 'exists' are present - this is the current state of the technology.
quests.explanation: 'Seems' and 'exists' are present simple forms. The sentence describes a current present reality.

quests.sentence: What will seem entirely ordinary to the next generation is currently being developed in research facilities.
quests.hint: 'Will seem' is the future - the ordinariness is a future state not yet reached.
quests.explanation: 'Will seem' is the future simple. The sentence makes a prediction about how future people will perceive current research.

quests.sentence: The prime minister resigned because she could no longer command the full confidence of her party.
quests.hint: 'Resigned' and 'could no longer command' are past - the resignation has happened.
quests.explanation: 'Resigned' is the simple past. 'Could no longer command' is the past modal. Both are completed past events.

quests.sentence: The prime minister continues to face considerable opposition and scepticism within her own parliamentary party.
quests.hint: 'Continues to face' is present - the internal opposition is an ongoing current situation.
quests.explanation: 'Continues' is the present simple. The sentence describes an ongoing current political situation.

quests.sentence: The prime minister will need the full support of her cabinet if she is to survive the confidence vote.
quests.hint: 'Will need' is the future - the vote is still ahead.
quests.explanation: 'Will need' is the future modal. 'If she is to survive the vote' is a future conditional.

quests.sentence: The discovery fundamentally transformed our entire understanding of how complex life first emerged on this planet.
quests.hint: 'Transformed' is past - the discovery has been made and its impact assessed.
quests.explanation: 'Transformed' is the simple past. The sentence describes a completed past discovery and its assessed impact.

quests.sentence: The discovery continues to transform the most fundamental questions scientists ask about the origins of life.
quests.hint: 'Continues to transform' is present - the transformative impact is ongoing.
quests.explanation: 'Continues' is the present simple. The sentence describes the ongoing present impact of an existing discovery.

quests.sentence: The discovery will transform everything we currently believe we know about the very beginnings of life on Earth.
quests.hint: 'Will transform' is the future - the full impact of the discovery is still to come.
quests.explanation: 'Will transform' is the future simple. The sentence predicts the future transformative impact of a current finding.
